Latowicz Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Strachomin, Poland

Demolished. Jews are first recorded near Latowicz in the second half of the 16th century, though settlement was initially restricted by a 1596 royal decree; more Jews arrived after 1826 under a Tsarist decree permitting settlement and construction. One local rabbi, Jakow Icchak Weinberg, was a grandson of the famous 'Seer of Lublin,' Rebbe Jakow Icchak Horowitz. By 1921, 416 Jews lived in the village, most murdered at Treblinka in 1942. The cemetery's history is largely undocumented, though it was probably established in the 19th century; local residents participated in its wartime destruction, repurposing tombstones as construction material and grinding wheels. Poland formally closed the cemetery by ministerial order in 1965, with documentation noting a final burial in 1943.
